You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does
  - The test constructs a symmetric tridiagonal eigen decomposition from:
    - main diagonal (length 5)
    - secondary diagonal (length 4)
  - It passes MathUtils.SAFE_MIN as the split tolerance, which is extremely small and effectively prevents splitting unless an off-diagonal is exactly zero.

- How the code executes on this input
  1. EigenDecompositionImpl(double[], double[], double)
     - Clones inputs and precomputes squaredSecondary.
     - Stores splitTolerance and calls decompose().
  2. decompose()
     - Allocates the working array work with length 6 * main.length (for 5, that’s 30 doubles).
     - computeGershgorinCircles() writes per-row Gershgorin lower/upper bounds into work starting at indices 4m and 5m, i.e., into [20..24] and [25..29], and computes minPivot.
     - findEigenvalues() is then called.
  3. findEigenvalues()
     - computeSplits() uses the tiny splitTolerance (SAFE_MIN) so no off-diagonal is considered small; hence there are no internal splits, and the whole matrix is treated as a single block of size n = 5.
     - In the default branch for n ≥ 4:
       - eigenvaluesRange(0, 5) reads the Gershgorin bounds from work[20..24] and work[25..29] to bound the spectra and chooses a shift.
       - ldlTDecomposition(lambda, 0, 5) packs the LDLᵀ data into work in a qd-like layout:
         - work[0], and for i = 1..4, work[4i - 2] (off-diagonal terms) and work[4i] (diagonal terms).
       - processGeneralBlock(5) is invoked to run the dqds iteration on this 5×5 block.

- Where the failure happens
  - Inside processGeneralBlock(int), the algorithm iteratively applies the dqds step:
    - It calls goodStep(i0, n0) (line 893) in a loop until the segment is fully processed.
  - With this dataset (no splits, n0 starts at 5), goodStep ends up accessing the internal work array with an index that is outside the valid range. This is an off-by-one/indexing error within the dqds step that uses the packed qd representation stored in work.
  - The exception reported (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) is consistent with this: all other array uses in the shown methods (Gershgorin circles, split computation, eigenvalue counts, LDLᵀ decomposition) respect array bounds for the given sizes, whereas the dqds iteration is the only stage performing complex index arithmetic near array boundaries and is known to be sensitive to loop bounds and last-element handling.

- Why this particular test triggers it
  - Passing SAFE_MIN as split tolerance ensures there are no early splits; the algorithm must process the entire 5×5 block through the general dqds path (processGeneralBlock → goodStep).
  - The combination of the specific tridiagonal values and the lack of splits drives goodStep into the faulty boundary case where it computes an index just beyond the segment (e.g., referencing the last qd entries with an offset), leading to out-of-bounds access on work.

- Conclusion
  - The ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException is caused by an incorrect index computation in the dqds iteration, specifically in EigenDecompositionImpl.goodStep(int, int), invoked from processGeneralBlock(int) at line 893. The work array is sized appropriately (6*m), and earlier stages write within bounds; the failure arises from off-by-one boundary handling in goodStep when processing the last elements of the qd representation for a block of size ≥ 4 with no splits.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does
  - The test constructs a symmetric tridiagonal eigen decomposition from:
    - main diagonal (length 5)
    - secondary diagonal (length 4)
  - It passes MathUtils.SAFE_MIN as the split tolerance, which is extremely small and effectively prevents splitting unless an off-diagonal is exactly zero.

- How the code executes on this input
  1. EigenDecompositionImpl(double[], double[], double)
     - Clones inputs and precomputes squaredSecondary.
     - Stores splitTolerance and calls decompose().
  2. decompose()
     - Allocates the working array work with length 6 * main.length (for 5, that’s 30 doubles).
     - computeGershgorinCircles() writes per-row Gershgorin lower/upper bounds into work starting at indices 4m and 5m, i.e., into [20..24] and [25..29], and computes minPivot.
     - findEigenvalues() is then called.
  3. findEigenvalues()
     - computeSplits() uses the tiny splitTolerance (SAFE_MIN) so no off-diagonal is considered small; hence there are no internal splits, and the whole matrix is treated as a single block of size n = 5.
     - In the default branch for n ≥ 4:
       - eigenvaluesRange(0, 5) reads the Gershgorin bounds from work[20..24] and work[25..29] to bound the spectra and chooses a shift.
       - ldlTDecomposition(lambda, 0, 5) packs the LDLᵀ data into work in a qd-like layout:
         - work[0], and for i = 1..4, work[4i - 2] (off-diagonal terms) and work[4i] (diagonal terms).
       - processGeneralBlock(5) is invoked to run the dqds iteration on this 5×5 block.

- Where the failure happens
  - Inside processGeneralBlock(int), the algorithm iteratively applies the dqds step:
    - It calls goodStep(i0, n0) (line 893) in a loop until the segment is fully processed.
  - With this dataset (no splits, n0 starts at 5), goodStep ends up accessing the internal work array with an index that is outside the valid range. This is an off-by-one/indexing error within the dqds step that uses the packed qd representation stored in work.
  - The exception reported (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) is consistent with this: all other array uses in the shown methods (Gershgorin circles, split computation, eigenvalue counts, LDLᵀ decomposition) respect array bounds for the given sizes, whereas the dqds iteration is the only stage performing complex index arithmetic near array boundaries and is known to be sensitive to loop bounds and last-element handling.

- Why this particular test triggers it
  - Passing SAFE_MIN as split tolerance ensures there are no early splits; the algorithm must process the entire 5×5 block through the general dqds path (processGeneralBlock → goodStep).
  - The combination of the specific tridiagonal values and the lack of splits drives goodStep into the faulty boundary case where it computes an index just beyond the segment (e.g., referencing the last qd entries with an offset), leading to out-of-bounds access on work.

- Conclusion
  - The ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException is caused by an incorrect index computation in the dqds iteration, specifically in EigenDecompositionImpl.goodStep(int, int), invoked from processGeneralBlock(int) at line 893. The work array is sized appropriately (6*m), and earlier stages write within bounds; the failure arises from off-by-one boundary handling in goodStep when processing the last elements of the qd representation for a block of size ≥ 4 with no splits.
